title: LINK std2 root-followed optimization
summary: Use backend ground-state energy and analytic gradient plus an APOC-followed std2 excitation correction; acquire Hessians by central differences of complete gradients.
gates: converged backend S0 energy, analytic Cartesian gradient and same-point Molden export
restricted closed-shell or unrestricted alpha/beta integer occupations; no implicit ROHF or spin-flip conversion
APOC spin-resolved transition-density matching; strict overlap and ambiguity gates
accepted geometries alone advance the APOC reference; derivative branches use a frozen central state
gradient = backend S0 gradient + central finite difference of only the std2 excitation eigenvalue
Hessian = central finite differences of the complete gradient, using the existing LINK Cartesian Hessian routine
upstream real4 eigenvalues and both derivative steps recorded; no numerical accuracy certification inferred
frozen atom ordering and Cartesian frame; SONIC or SYCART optimizer variables
coordinate_policy: The existing LINK optimizer uses SONIC or SYCART. Excitation gradients use central Cartesian displacements in the frozen frame; complete Cartesian gradients feed the existing central Hessian stencil and symmetry projection.
backend_policy: The ground-state backend owns S0 energy/gradient and orbitals. External std2 supplies excitation eigenpairs. APOC owns spin-resolved root identity. LINK composes energies/gradients and uses its existing optimizer and gradient-difference Hessian. No new ground-state gradient or TDA kernel implementation.
